_comment: High-tier case study, 0017's tier partner (10 conversations touching the ruling -- the widest spread of any ruling in the census). Built the same way as case_study_decisions_0017.json, but see the boilerplate caveat below before trusting the raw n_conversations=10 figure at face value.
ruling_title_in_decisions_md: The registry is three-tier: program -> project -> repo
census_method: scan_all_decisions.py --root against the 2026-08-18 backup; 0012 hit 10 conversations, 76 mentions total
boilerplate_caveat: Five of the ten conversations that match (local_1c846ab9, local_a9c1841b, local_602a1aed, local_8eb98916, local_d5156fb3) contain the identical block '=== THREE-TIER REGISTRY -- program > project > repo (DECISIONS 0012) === id scheme: id (every tier is a link target; project_link always holds an id) ===' verbatim -- this reads as a pinned reference header pasted at the start of unrelated sessions (likely a schema/context primer), not organic per-conversation discussion of the ruling. Counting these as five independent 'conversations about 0012' would overstate the story's real cross-conversation richness. The timeline below is built only from conversations where 0012 is actually being reasoned about, not just quoted as a header -- five genuinely substantive conversations, not ten.

timeline.event: invoked as an already-settled architectural argument against filesystem mirroring
timeline.speaker: assistant
timeline.quoted_substring: DECISIONS 0012 put program->project->repo in the **registry** precisely so the filesystem doesn't have [to mirror it]
timeline.note: This is the same conversation (local_2beef53e) that drafted DECISIONS 0017 the same morning, and here it is nine days BEFORE the 0018-0043 numbering block even started -- 0012 is already load-bearing history by 2026-07-21, confirming it predates this transcript's earliest capture window.

timeline.event: reaffirmed minutes later against a concrete folder-structure proposal
timeline.speaker: assistant
timeline.quoted_substring: Program->project->repo stays in the registry, where DECISIONS 0012 put it, rather than being duplicated in folders where the two can silently disagree.
timeline.note: Same conversation as seq 1, eight minutes later -- the ruling directly shapes a concrete design decision (one-level folder hierarchy, hierarchy stays in the registry, not on disk).

timeline.event: listed as one of a block of rulings a build round implemented and that remain live
timeline.speaker: assistant
timeline.quoted_substring: (23b5ffa -- build_inventory now reads the deposited census, not a folder walk). DECISIONS 0012-0016 hold the rulings this brief implemented and remain live.
timeline.note: Four days after seq 1/2, different conversation -- confirms 0012 was actually built against, not just discussed in the abstract.

timeline.event: used to characterize a repo-lineage question as program-shaped rather than single-project
timeline.speaker: assistant
timeline.quoted_substring: The lineage is program-shaped (DECISIONS 0012 logic -- a portfolio of substantial repos, not one project): v1 proto (10 threads) -> A[rmory...]
timeline.note: Same day as seq 3, different conversation -- 0012's tiering logic gets applied to classify a specific ambiguous repo lineage.

timeline.event: diagnosed as the source of a real, previously-invisible bug
timeline.speaker: user/assistant
timeline.quoted_substring: a real 0012 gap rather than a patch. [...] Under 0012 the deposits are repo-named, so the repo tier is invisible.
timeline.note: This is the SAME conversation that discovers the DECISIONS 0016->0018 gap and ratifies 0017 later that day (see case_study_decisions_0017.json seq 4) -- 0012's story physically overlaps with both 0017's and 0018's in this one session.

timeline.speaker: user
timeline.quoted_substring: because all four evidence producers were blind to the repo tier under DECISIONS 0012. That blocker is now fixed in the working tree.
timeline.note: A different conversation, same morning as seq 5 -- the fix diagnosed in local_e9841a20 gets landed here.

timeline.event: cited retrospectively as a live ruling a stale document is missing
timeline.speaker: assistant
timeline.quoted_substring: the three-tier registry (0012), estate-scoped visibility (0025), knowledge documents (0026), render-time reads (0027)
timeline.note: Six days after seq 5/6 -- same audit pass referenced in 0026's case study seq 5.

timeline.event: used to explain a legacy-id naming collision as a versioning artefact rather than a bug
timeline.speaker: assistant
timeline.quoted_substring: l5gn-os is precisely the id that changed meaning between generations (0012's program tier, 0017's reset).
timeline.note: Same conversation as seq 7, later that day -- 0012 and 0017 are explicitly linked together again, this time to explain a naming quirk, not a design decision.

cross_check_against_decisions_md.decisions_md_states: The registry is three-tier: program -> project -> repo
cross_check_against_decisions_md.transcript_evidence: Consistent throughout -- every substantive mention (seq 1-8) treats the tiering as settled and applies it, never revisits or contradicts it. No contradiction found.
cross_check_against_decisions_md.note: Unlike 0017, no draft/ratify gap is visible for 0012 in this transcript window -- it appears to already be settled doctrine from the earliest conversation available (2026-07-21), consistent with it being one of the earlier-numbered rulings.

why_this_is_a_good_benchmark_item: It's the deliberate 'high volume, but check your sources' trap: the raw n_conversations=10 signal is inflated by five conversations that only contain a pasted reference header, not discussion -- a good synthesis answer should notice and exclude the boilerplate, not report all ten as equally substantive.

Its real story (5 substantive conversations, 6 days) is comparable in size to 0018's, despite the raw scan numbers making it look far bigger than 0018 or 0026 -- testing whether a model's account of 'how much was this really discussed' tracks the evidence rather than the scan's surface count.

It intersects BOTH 0017's story (seq 5, seq 8) and touches the same conversation as 0018's audit moment (seq 5 is local_e9841a20, same as 0018's seq 4 and 0017's seq 4) -- a model given all three case studies should be able to describe 2026-07-27's local_e9841a20 session as the point where three separate rulings' stories converge.
